title: Introduction; mother's family and background
description: Dale Anderson introduces the interview at St. Mary's, Idaho, in July 1975. Mamie Reeser gives her own vital details and those of her mother, Ella Kavanagh Modern, born in Michigan in 1874. Ella worked as a schoolteacher, hat-shop and cafe owner, midwife, and homesteader near Marble Creek after coming to Idaho with her father.

title: Father; brothers; husband; children
description: Mamie describes her father, Edwin Modern, a Tennessee-born lumberjack whose family settled on the Rockford reservation before moving to Harrison, where he met Ella at her cafe. She names her two brothers, her husband Stanley Reesor of Phillipsburg, Kansas, and their two children, Andy and Candy, along with their education, jobs, and three granddaughters.

title: Life history; schooling; wartime marriage
description: Mamie gives a rundown of her life: schooling in Plummer and St. Mary's, pep club, work at Robeson's, the telephone office, and JCPenney, then marriage in Colorado in 1942. She describes life at Camp Carson and Fort Lewis, returning to St. Mary's in 1945, raising the children, leading Scout and Camp Fire groups, and starting work at Davis Link in 1959 to fund college.

title: Children's college; mother's homestead story; childbirth
description: Mamie explains how an endowment and her wages sent Andy to the College of Idaho and then the university, while Candy went via junior college. She recalls her mother Ella homesteading alone on Marble Creek, riding twelve miles into the mountains to keep the claim, and the cabin summer of Mamie's childhood. She also touches on her own home birth by midwife and her children's hospital births.

title: Small-town life; recreation; married life in Colorado
description: Mamie contrasts friendly small towns with impersonal cities and notes St. Mary's growth and newcomers. She recalls childhood swimming, tennis, and sledding, her children's clubs and sports, and her courtship of dances and shows. During the war in Colorado she and Stanley toured Garden of the Gods, Pikes Peak, Manitou Springs, and other sights.

title: Married life; working mothers; homemaking
description: Mamie describes her happy marriage, two good children, breast cancer in 1967 and 1969, and pastimes like Elks parties and a twenty-year bridge club. She argues mothers should stay home until children reach high school age, explains she worked only to fund college with Stanley's mother's help, and mentions sewing and canning.

title: Family gatherings; church; media; family decisions
description: The extended family gathers every Thanksgiving at her home and Christmas at her brother's, a tradition from her father. Her family attended Presbyterian church and her daughter now attends a Lutheran church, though Mamie never joined. She lists her newspapers, magazines, favorite western and family TV shows, and says family decisions are made by discussion.

title: Advice; more about mother; Depression and war
description: Mamie advises young women moving to small towns to be friendly and active. She adds details about her stylish mother Ella, her cafe, hat shop, Rebekah honors, and midwife work with local doctors. She recalls Depression hardship and the war years, including Stanley being named father of the year at Fort Lewis with toddler Andy.

title: Travel; vacations; closing
description: Mamie mentions trips to San Francisco, Las Vegas, Reno, and Canada, a family visit to Michigan, and regular visits to Andy in Seattle and relatives near Boise. She suggests her brother the Ford dealer would be a good interview subject, then the interview closes.
